sources.entry: skhd - Simple hotkey daemon for macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/koekeishiya/skhd)

summary.one_liner: skhd is a simple hotkey daemon for macOS that binds keyboard shortcuts to shell commands via a text-file DSL, with live config reloading.
summary.what_it_does: skhd runs in the background on macOS and listens for key events, executing shell commands when a defined hotkey is pressed. Hotkeys are declared in a plain text config file (default locations: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/skhd/skhdrc, $HOME/.config/skhd/skhdrc, or $HOME/.skhdrc) using a simple DSL. The config hotloads, so edits apply while skhd is running, and skhd --reload triggers a manual reload. The README also describes modal hotkey systems, application-specific bindings, a blacklist of applications, use of media keys as hotkeys, and synthesizing key presses and text via command-line flags. It can be installed as a launchd service. Only one instance runs at a time, enforced by a pid-file in /tmp.
use_cases: bind global keyboard shortcuts to shell commands on macOS
launch or switch applications with a keystroke
set different hotkeys for specific applications
remap or pass through keys in selected apps
automate key presses or typed text from the command line
how_to_run: git clone (Source install; repository URL not shown in README)
notable: Hotkeys defined in a plain text file with a simple DSL, hotloaded while running
Modal hotkey system and application-specific bindings
Blacklist applications via .blacklist and include partial config files via .load
Can use media keys as hotkeys and synthesize key presses or text (-k, -t flags)
Runs as a launchd service with --install-service / --start-service
caveats: Maintenance mode: only critical issues affecting core functionality will be addressed; the README points to a Zig port by Jackie Li for feature expansion
Requires granting accessibility API access and restarting the app; Secure Keyboard Entry must be disabled to receive key events
Source build requires xcode-8 command-line tools (per README)
